newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: Seoul allows five local firms to invest in N.Korea.
newsitem.headline: Seoul allows five local firms to invest in N.Korea.

text.p: South Korea on Friday allowed five local companies to invest in North Korea as part of steps to seek detente and build up mutual trust, the National Unification Ministry said.

The move, which also allows a telecommunications company to pursue a joint project with a North Korean partner, comes only four days before the two Koreas are due to hold talks along with the United States and China.
The five include Samsung Electronics Co, South Korea's largest electronics company, and Kolon International, a leading manufacturer of textile products, a ministry statement said.

"These steps are taken in accordance with the government's consistent policy to increase economic exchanges and cooperation to achieve reconcilation between the South and North and build up mutual trust," it said.
Senior officials of the two Koreas, the United States and China are due to meet in New York next Tuesday to set a date, venue and agenda for four-nation peace talks.

The four-party talks, first proposed by U.S. President Bill Clinton and South Korean President Kim Young-sam in April 1996, are aimed at hammering out a permanent peace settlement to replace the armistice that ended the 1950-53 Korean War.
